headingText.html: Signet Artists serve milestone birthdays and anniversaries, engagement dinners, holiday gatherings at home, club celebrations just to name a few.

props.title: Ensemble sizes, and how they change the vibe.

props.html: In our experience, most hosts guess too big.

rows.text: One voice and a guitar or piano in the corner of a dinner makes the evening feel thoughtfully planned, and it fits into a home without moving the furniture.
A volume people easily talk across at arrival and dinner, with the range to lift the last hour if that's where things are headed.
The one that gets people dancing without a stage: usually guitar or keys, bass and drums. Or a fuller, still laid-back jazz ensemble.

props.eyebrow: what kind of night do you want?
props.title: three common entertainment choices for private parties.
props.lede: Most of the requests we get look like one of these three.

rows.text: Jazz standards on upright bass and guitar, at a level you can talk across, for an hour or from arrival through dessert. Book the jazz duo, or a solo guitarist for a smaller guest list.

rows.term: The cocktail party that ends in dancing
rows.text: A trio through drinks that becomes the band that gets people dancing. Where dancing is a maybe rather than the plan, an acoustic duo covers the night.

A 40th birthday, a notable anniversary or an engagement dinner. The band plays around the toast and any surprise, with an announcement microphone ready from sound check. Planning a proposal? See live music for proposals.

props.title: a birthday big enough to deserve a band.
props.lede: For most birthdays, a restaurant with family and friends is a perfect night. But sometimes the celebration is so important that the whole night is built to cheer on the guest of honor.

image.alt: Guests with their arms in the air at a packed party in a bar with a chandelier.

rows.text: The ones that run latest and hit hardest. A trio fills a floor without a stage, and a DJ keeps guests dancing to the end of the night.
Two parties in one evening: guests arrive and eat, then let loose. A trio or quartet works well.
More often a seated dinner with a toast. Live players at a lower volume, with a song list built from the years the guest of honor cares about.
Earlier and warmer, with more family and more of it seated. A solo player or a jazz duo holds the evening from arrival through dessert.

rows.text: No extra cost for travel. Holiday gatherings in homes compete with office parties in the city for the same dates.
Parties tend to be smaller, in homes and clubs where guests sit close to the band, so solo and duo are the sizes to ask about first.
More of the private calendar runs around wedding weekends and resort terraces, and the acoustic duo is the size booked most.

props.html: Castle Pines, Castle Rock and Evergreen are inside the no-travel-charge area too, so a party at a house in any of the three is quoted the same as Denver.

props.title: 9 parties with details of their own.

rows.text: An engagement party is often the first time the two families are in one place. A duo works well, and the same duo can play the wedding’s cocktail hour later on.
A solo guitarist is a lovely touch for an afternoon shower, and it's an easy way to add something besides the games.
A singer and guitarist is a great choice when the grandparents and the graduate’s friends are all at the same party.
We can do anything from a solo guitarist on the patio to a trio on the lawn.
We can plan the surprise entrance with the music and put the toast on a microphone.

Most anniversary parties are dinners, and there’s usually one song that matters more than the rest. If it’s a surprise the kids are throwing, or a vow renewal with ceremony music, we can plan for that too.
A retirement party might be thrown by the company or the family, and there are usually a few speeches. We’d suggest jazz standards, which tend to work well for a mix of ages.
We can bring a DJ, a party band or live band karaoke, in costume if you like.
We can bring a Christmas jazz duo or trio for dinner, or a party band or DJ for a house full of people, whether your party falls in Thanksgiving week or on New Year’s Eve.

props.title: What hosts often ask when they get in touch.

props.html: Stage sizes, electrical concerns and sound needs are on the technical page.

image.alt: A hand raising a glass of champagne for a toast.

items.q: What does a band for a dinner party cost?
items.a: It depends on how many musicians and how long, and for a dinner party that's usually one or two musicians rather than the full band many hosts picture. We quote each date one-by-one. What's published on our pricing page is a general market-view of what live music costs in Denver, Colorado. Let us know what you're planning and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price.

items.q: How much space and power does the band need at home?
items.a: A solo musician needs about 6 by 4 feet, a duo about 8 by 6 and a trio about 12 by 8, and none of them needs a stage. One dedicated 20-amp outlet usually covers a solo, duo or trio, and a quartet may need two. The most common problem we see is sharing power with the caterer's warmers, so it's a good idea to check with your caterer ahead of time.

items.q: How long does setup take, and what does a club ask for?
items.a: Setup takes about 45 minutes for a solo and up to 90 for a quartet, before guests arrive, and strike is 30 to 60 minutes at the end. Tell us where to park and which door to use. Clubs and managed buildings usually ask for a certificate of insurance, and we can send whatever paperwork the venue needs. Just let us know.

At dinner, we'll keep the music low enough that you can talk without raising your voice. If there's dancing later on, we can turn things up. If there's a shared wall, a close neighbor or a club sound policy, let us know when you book and we'll plan the night around it.

items.q: Can you play outdoors at a home?
items.a: Yes. We'll need a spot that's covered, level and dry with power nearby, plus a plan for moving indoors that we'll work out with you beforehand. Colorado evenings can cool off fast, and instruments and electronics don't like the cold or the wet.

props.title: Tell us about the party, and we'll recommend the act for it.
props.lede: Whether you're picturing a solo musician or a full band, just reach out and we'll help you find the right live entertainment.
props.note: Want photos or video of the party to keep? We can add them to your booking.
